Here is a factual research note on the news event: *“Rescue of 3,595 Yazidis from ISIS,”* based on current reporting.

---

### Key Facts

- **Total abducted in August 2014**: 6,417 Yazidis from Sinjar and surrounding areas by ISIS. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  
- **Number rescued so far**: 3,595 individuals. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  
- **Number still missing / unknown fate**: 2,822 individuals. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Sources and Sources’ Status

- **Primary/Official Source**: Statements by **Hussein Qaidy** (also spelled “Qaidi”), the director of the *Office for Rescuing Kidnapped Yazidis* (Kurdistan Region). He provided these figures in recent interviews with Iraqi and Kurdish media outlets. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  
- **Independent Media & Observers**: Multiple outlets—BasNews, Waʿa (Iraqi news agency), IshtarTV, Kurdish 24—independently reported the same statistics based on Qaidy’s statement. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Breakdown by Demographics & Location

- Among the **missing (2,822)**:  
  • More than half are women and girls.  
  • A significant number are children. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  

- Regarding the **rescued (3,595)**:  
  • Majority were found in **Syria**.  
  • Many missing are believed to remain in Syrian territory—especially in **Al-Hol camp**, or with families of ISIS members in Iraq—and some may have been moved out of Iraq and Syria. ([basnews.com](https://www.basnews.com/ar/babat/923070?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Context & Ongoing Efforts

- **Time elapsed**: Over 11 years have passed since the Sinjar attack in August 2014. ([ishtartv.com](https://ishtartv.com/viewarticle%2C121933.html?utm_source=openai))  
- **Current operations**: The rescue efforts are active; the office continues to follow up leads, especially in Syrian territory. ([video-agencyia.iq](https://video-agencyia.iq/EN/Detail/8283?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Assessment: Is This a "Significant Humanitarian Outcome"?

- This is **not just an announcement or pledge**. The rescue of 3,595 Yazidis is a **measured outcome**—people have been freed. It is concrete and verifiable.  
- Yet, with 2,822 still missing, the crisis is **ongoing**, so while this is a major achievement, the total goal (identifying/rescuing all missing) has not yet been realized.

---

If you like, I can try to locate official UN or international NGO reports confirming these figures, to further triangulate this information.

Here’s a factual research note on news of a **new mental health facility in Greater St. Louis**, based on available sources. I found no credible evidence that a new residential treatment facility *open now* in November 2026 has opened under that exact description; several related projects are in planning or construction. Below is a summary of what is confirmed, what is in progress, and what is under discussion.

---

## What is confirmed / in progress

1. **Children’s mental health hospital & outpatient center (Webster Groves)**  
   - A new 77-bed pediatric mental health hospital is being built on the KVC Missouri Children’s Mental Wellness Campus in Webster Groves, Missouri. ([stlmag.com](https://www.stlmag.com/health/pediatric-mental-health-hospital-webster-groves/?utm_source=openai))  
   - It is a joint venture between *St. Louis Children’s Hospital* and *KVC Health Systems*. ([stlouischildrenskvc.org](https://www.stlouischildrenskvc.org/visit-us/?utm_source=openai))  
   - The facility will offer four levels of care: acute inpatient treatment, psychiatric residential care, partial hospitalization program (PHP), and intensive outpatient program (IOP). ([stlmag.com](https://www.stlmag.com/health/pediatric-mental-health-hospital-webster-groves/?utm_source=openai))  
   - It is aimed at youth aged 6-18. ([stlmag.com](https://www.stlmag.com/health/pediatric-mental-health-hospital-webster-groves/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Construction began in spring 2025; “topping out” (completion of the structural framework) was reported in December 2025. ([bjc.org](https://www.bjc.org/news/stl-npr-construction-underway-77-bed-webster-groves-pediatric-mental-health-hospital?utm_source=openai))  
   - The opening is scheduled for **late 2026**. ([stlmag.com](https://www.stlmag.com/health/pediatric-mental-health-hospital-webster-groves/?utm_source=openai))  

2. **Preferred Family Healthcare clinic in Jennings**  
   - A separate facility is being built in Jennings, Missouri: a $13 million clinic including outpatient and inpatient behavioral health care, a residential treatment facility for adults with substance use disorders, outpatient psychiatry services, primary medical care, and an onsite pharmacy. ([pfh.org](https://pfh.org/preferred-family-healthcare-building-13m-clinic-in-jennings/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Groundbreaking was December 2025; completion expected September 2026. ([pfh.org](https://pfh.org/preferred-family-healthcare-building-13m-clinic-in-jennings/?utm_source=openai))  

3. **SSM Health SLU Behavioral Health Unit**  
   - In December 2025, SSM Health Saint Louis University Hospital opened a renovated Behavioral Health Unit in Bordley Tower with 42 private beds for inpatient behavioral health treatment. ([ssmhealth.com](https://www.ssmhealth.com/SSMHealth/media/Documents/conditions-treatments/emergency-trauma-services/emergency-perspectives-magazine.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What is **not** confirmed / appears inaccurate

- I found **no reliable source** confirming that a new residential mental health treatment facility has *opened* very recently (as of November 14, 2026) in Greater St. Louis for adults, matching the candidate headline exactly.
- An article found (a press-release) describes “St. Louis Mental Health Opens New Residential Mental Health Treatment Facility” in Winfield, Missouri. However, I could not locate independent corroboration of that claim beyond the press-release. ([press.central-chart.com](https://press.central-chart.com/press-release/2026-11-13/38408/st-louis-mental-health-opens-new-residential-mental-health-treatment-facility-serving-greater-st-louis?utm_source=openai))  
    - Details in that release: facility at 350 Birkhead Rd in Winfield, accepting adults 18+, same-day admissions, treatment for mood, anxiety, trauma, etc. But the only source I saw is the press release itself. ([press.central-chart.com](https://press.central-chart.com/press-release/2026-11-13/38408/st-louis-mental-health-opens-new-residential-mental-health-treatment-facility-serving-greater-st-louis?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completed / Measured Outcomes vs. Plans and Announcements

| Facility / Project | Status as of Nov 14, 2026 | Type of Announcement or Outcome |
|--------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Webster Groves pediatric hospital & outpatient center | **Under construction; expected to open late 2026** | Plan / development / construction announcement; no opening yet. ([stlmag.com](https://www.stlmag.com/health/pediatric-mental-health-hospital-webster-groves/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Jennings PFH clinic | **Not yet open; expected Sept 2026** | Groundbreaking and projected completion date provided. ([pfh.org](https://pfh.org/preferred-family-healthcare-building-13m-clinic-in-jennings/?utm_source=openai)) |
| SLU Behavioral Health Unit | **Already opened** (December 2025) | Completed renovation and opened 42-bed unit for adult inpatient behavioral health evaluation, stabilization, etc. ([ssmhealth.com](https://www.ssmhealth.com/SSMHealth/media/Documents/conditions-treatments/emergency-trauma-services/emergency-perspectives-magazine.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| Winfield adult residential facility press release | **Claimed to be open** per press release | Press release asserts opening; lacking independent verification beyond the source itself. ([press.central-chart.com](https://press.central-chart.com/press-release/2026-11-13/38408/st-louis-mental-health-opens-new-residential-mental-health-treatment-facility-serving-greater-st-louis?utm_source=openai)) |

---

## Conclusion: What actually happened

- As of November 14, 2026, a major **new pediatric mental health facility (77-bed hospital + outpatient services)** is slated to open in Webster Groves late in 2026. It is **not yet open**. ([stlmag.com](https://www.stlmag.com/health/pediatric-mental-health-hospital-webster-groves/?utm_source=openai))  
- Also under development are other behavioral / clinic facilities. The one in Jennings, for example, is a clinic project not yet completed. ([pfh.org](https://pfh.org/preferred-family-healthcare-building-13m-clinic-in-jennings/?utm_source=openai))  
- The press release about a facility at Winfield claims that it “has officially opened” a residential mental health treatment facility for adults. But there appear to be **no independent sources** confirming that actual opening or usage outcomes beyond that press release. ([press.central-chart.com](https://press.central-chart.com/press-release/2026-11-13/38408/st-louis-mental-health-opens-new-residential-mental-health-treatment-facility-serving-greater-st-louis?utm_source=openai))  

---

If you want, I can check for official state or county health department records to verify whether the Winfield facility is in fact open and operating. Would you like me to do that?

Here’s a factual research note on the event **“950 seedlings planted for forest recovery / 950 Bibit Ditanam, Pemulihan Hutan Lindung Liang Anggang Dimulai”**, with confirmation of what actually happened, based on primary and independent sources:

---

## What Happened

- On **Friday, November 13, 2026**, a planting event took place in the protected forest area **Hutan Lindung Liang Anggang**, Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, Indonesia. During this event, **950 seedlings** were planted as part of the initial stage of forest recovery. ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- The planted seedlings were of fruit tree species—namely **mangga (mango) and nangka (jackfruit)**. ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- The event was led by the Provincial Forestry Agency (**Dinas Kehutanan Provinsi Kalimantan Selatan**), headed by **Fathimatuzzahra**, together with the Forest Management Unit (**Kesatuan Pengelolaan Hutan, KPH Kayu Tangi**), and about **150 personnel** participated (forestry officers, KPH personnel, local environmental volunteers). ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Context and Additional Details

- The planting was part of a larger effort to rehabilitate forest vegetation and to improve water system (“tata air”) in the protected area, which has been under ecological pressure. ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- Alongside planting, there is a plan to construct semi-permanent canals (by a synergy between Forestry Department, PUPR - Public Works and Spatial Planning, and Balai Wilayah Sungai Kalimantan III) to maintain water availability, particularly during dry seasons. ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- The full canal in the area spans about **9.5 kilometers**, of which approximately **2.2 km** has already been addressed in this first stage, with planting frequency roughly every **5 meters** along canal edges. ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- The plan also includes developing the Liang Anggang area for **“productive and sustainable” uses**—including ecotourism (like fishing), while preserving its primary function as a protected forest. ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completed/Measured Outcome vs. Other Announcements

- This is a **completed action**, not merely a pledge or future plan: 950 seedlings were physically planted on a specific date (13 Nov 2026). ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- It is distinguished from earlier announcements concerning the **Liang Anggang seedling nursery (Persemaian Liang Anggang)**, which were about establishing large-scale seedling production and facility infrastructure. Those earlier events involved building a nursery with capacity for millions of seedlings per year, not this specific planting event. ([diskominfomc.kalselprov.go.id](https://diskominfomc.kalselprov.go.id/2024/09/03/pusat-produksi-bibit-menteri-lhk-tinjau-persemaian-liang-anggang-di-kalsel/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent Corroboration & Sources

- The primary reporting on this particular planting event comes from *Kalimantan Update* with detailed coverage (date, participants, species, etc.). ([kalimantanupdate.com](https://www.kalimantanupdate.com/12987/950-bibit-ditanam-pemulihan-hutan-lindung-liang-anggang-dimulai/?utm_source=openai))  
- I found no other independent media reports (e.g. national outlets or NGOs) that independently confirmed this specific event (950 seedlings in Liang Anggang on Nov 13, 2026) outside of *Kalimantan Update*. As of this research, it appears the story is currently singular in coverage.  

---

Let me know if you’d like further verification—such as photographs, statements from government sources, survival rates of these seedlings, or follow-up monitoring.

Here’s what I found regarding the claim “China targets clean energy to cover all new power demand by 2030”:

---

### What the official sources say

1. **Plan for a “clean, low-carbon, secure and efficient new energy system by 2030”**  
   A plan jointly issued by China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the National Energy Administration (NEA) in June 2026 aims to establish such a system by 2030. It includes targets such as coal and oil consumption peaking, non-fossil energy making up 25 % of total energy consumption, and wind & solar exceeding 50 % of installed power generation capacity. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202606/25/content_WS6a3d2904c6d00ca5f9a0bcde.html?utm_source=openai))

2. **Goal for non-fossil electricity share**  
   In August 2026, China unveiled the five-year plan (2026-2030) for the power sector, setting a target that non-fossil fuels will provide **50 % of the country’s electricity generation** by 2030. Under that plan, over 2.8 billion kilowatts (2,800 GW) of new energy (mostly wind & solar) capacity is to be integrated into the grid. The plan also calls for a charging infrastructure network capable of supporting over 110 million electric vehicles. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202608/04/content_WS6a714cd2c6d00ca5f9a0c883.html?utm_source=openai))

3. **How this compares to current/near-term figures**  
   As of mid-2026, China had non-fossil sources contributing about **21.7 %** of its total energy consumption, and the combined capacity of wind and solar reached ~1.84 billion kilowatts (1,840 GW). ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202610/21/content_WS6ad865e6c6d00ca5f9a0ddec.html?utm_source=openai))

---

### Independent/external assessments & nuance

- A commentary by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) points out that while these targets mark continued progress and stronger signals from Beijing, they *do not explicitly say* that *all new electricity demand* must be met by clean energy sources. In other words, the goals are ambitious but leave room for fossil fuels to still expand in absolute terms if overall demand grows significantly. ([energyandcleanair.org](https://energyandcleanair.org/chinas-new-energy-plan-leaves-emissions-loose/?utm_source=openai))

- Reuters, via MarketScreener, confirms China’s target of 50 % electricity from nonfossil fuels by 2030, noting it is up from 42.3 % for 2025. It also reports that the new plan includes binding targets on renewables integration and increasing electrification via EV infrastructure. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/china-targeting-half-of-power-from-non-fossil-sources-by-2030-ce7f5fd9db8cf727?utm_source=openai))

---

### What the claim **does and does not** reflect

- **Does**:  
   • A real, official target has been set — by 2030, 50 % of China’s *electricity generation* should come from non-fossil sources. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202608/04/content_WS6a714cd2c6d00ca5f9a0c883.html?utm_source=openai))  
   • There is a plan for adding large amounts of renewable capacity (wind, solar, etc.), and for building supporting infrastructure. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202607/23/content_WS6a617ed3c6d00ca5f9a0c5e8.html?utm_source=openai))  

- **Does not**:  
   • The plan does **not** explicitly say clean energy must supply *all* future new power demand (i.e. 100 % of growth).  
   • It does *not* ban new fossil power; rather, it aims to reduce its share or intensity, improve system flexibility, and peak fossil-fuel use. There remains implicit flexibility for fossil fuel generation to continue in some form.  
   • As of now, the target is forward-looking (to be achieved by 2030), not a completed outcome.

---

### Conclusion: What the evidence supports

The factual conclusion is that China has **officially committed** under its 2026-2030 energy plan to have non-fossil fuels supply 50 % of its electricity by 2030, with an expanded renewables generation base. However, there is no credible evidence that China has committed to having *all* new power demand (i.e., 100 % of incremental demand) met exclusively by clean energy by 2030. That appears to be an overstatement, or at best, an interpretation not backed by the official texts.

If you like, I can dig for whether any speech, secondary government announcement, or NGO report uses language closer to “all new demand,” which could have led to the version in your candidate news headline.
